stance_taxonomy.recognition: treats parental alienation as a real, assessable clinical phenomenon; conducts PA-specific assessment, facilitation, parenting-coordination or reunification work; typically PASG / Family-Bridges-aligned or aligned with SA recognition-camp jurisprudence anchored in T.L.D v B.G
stance_taxonomy.critique: argues PA construct (especially Gardner's SAP) is operationalised against DV / GBV survivors; advocates DV/trauma-informed alternatives, child-voice safeguards, and tighter regulation of expert witnesses
stance_taxonomy.middle: engages both alienating-behaviour and family-violence frames; differential-diagnosis or systemic / multi-family approach; parenting-coordination / mediation focus; not aligned with PASG and not in the abolitionist critique camp
stance_taxonomy.not_publicly_confirmed: included for institutional record completeness; PA-specific stance not in primary sources

africa_context_notes.ZA: HPCSA Professional Board for Psychology (clinical/counselling/educational/forensic). SACSSP regulates social workers (Act 110/1978). Parenting coordinators accredited via NABFAM (https://nabfam.co.za/) + voluntary associations FAMAC, KAFAM, SAAM, Family Life Centre, Social Justice Association of Mediators. SA Standards of Practice for Forensic Assessments drafted 2021 (Martalas-chaired task force). Leading judicial citation T.L.D v B.G [2023] ZAGPJHC 801 (Adams J) — named clinical psychologist Leonard Carr, parenting coordinators Dr Lynette Roux + Adv Vicky Olivier, father's expert Christie Els. Children's Act 38/2005 statutory frame.
africa_context_notes.KE: Counsellors and Psychologists Board (CPRB) under Counsellors and Psychologists Act 2014 (https://cprb.ecitizen.go.ke/). Parallel associations KCPA (~7,000 members) + KPsyA. Children Act 2022 codifies best-interests-of-the-child paramount. No institutional PA-position statement publicly issued.
africa_context_notes.NG: Nigeria Association of Clinical Psychologists (NACP, https://nacp.com.ng/). Federal frame under Nigerian Psychological Association / Federal Ministry of Health. Family-court PA via Matrimonial Causes Act + Child's Rights Act, best-interests standard. No public PA-position from NACP / NPA located.
africa_context_notes.EG: Psychologists licensed via Ministry of Health + Egyptian Psychiatric Association. State body NCCM (Presidential Decree 54/1988) — Child Helpline 16000 + psychological-support / family-counselling unit + Safe Child Unit (six-governorate pilot Jan 2026). NCCM publicly opposed 2016 draft personal-status reforms expanding non-custodial parent access on women-safety grounds (Mada Masr 28 Dec 2016) — critique-leaning institutional stance on PA-adjacent custody reform.

practitioners.stance_source: NCCM policy frame combines (a) psychological support, family counselling, behaviour modification, speech therapy via Child Rescue Department + Helpline 16000 and (b) NCCM's 2016 public position (per Mada Masr 28 Dec 2016 https://www.madamasr.com/en/2016/12/28/feature/society/egypts-child-custody-laws-how-to-reform/ ) opposing draft personal-status reforms that would have expanded non-custodial parent access on women-safety grounds — placing NCCM in middle / critique-leaning position on PA-adjacent custody-access reform. Specific direct PA-position notice not publicly confirmed.
programs_or_publications: Child Helpline 16000
Safe Child Unit (six-governorate pilot announced Jan 2026)
Psychological-support and family-counselling unit
Egyptian Personal Status Law reform engagement
practitioners.hook: Egypt's standing statutory child-rights / family-policy body and state operator of Child Helpline psychological-support unit — only institutional Egyptian addressee with both a public stance on PA-adjacent custody-access reform (critique-leaning per 2016 Mada Masr) and operational psychological-support capacity.
practitioners.notes: No named Egyptian PA clinical psychologist located within time-budget public-web search; NCCM is the institutional anchor.
